278392014_de284d9a.text: As the primary source of norepinephrine (NE) in the brain, the locus coeruleus (LC) regulates arousal, avoidance and stress responses1,2

278392014_25d93ab8.text: . We define peri-LC anatomy using viral tracing and combine single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics to molecularly define both LCNE and peri-LC cell types. We identify several neuronal cell types which underlie peri-LC functional diversity using a series of complementary neural circuit approaches in behaving mice. Our findings indicate that LC and peri-LC neurons are transcriptionally, functionally, and anatomically heterogenous neuronal populations which modulate arousal and avoidance states.
